items.title: GTA VI's painted-on tunnel keeps fooling drivers
items.summary: Kotaku reports players keep crashing at speed into a fake tunnel painted on a wall in Vice City's Decor District near Stockyard — a realistic mural, in the style of a Looney Tunes gag, that looks like a real tunnel entrance until the moment you hit it, with clips of the wrecks piling up on social media since launch.

items.title: Panini is turning GTA VI's in-game cards into real trading cards
items.summary: Push Square reports Panini is making real-life GTA VI trading cards in partnership with Rockstar, based on the game's fictional sports teams and the collectible cards players find around Leonida: 480 cards across 16 sets, sold in four-pack boxes with rare team-colour parallels to chase, due out in December with no price announced yet.

items.title: Why GTA VI's Chapter 1 chores make its ending hurt
items.summary: Polygon argues the early house chores — Jason fixing steps and a railing, buying groceries, painting and building furniture for Lucia's return — are what make the Chapter 1 ending land: masked attackers searching for the bag burn the home down around Lucia's fight, destroying the crib, the coffee table they built together and Jason's keepsakes, and leaving the couple in a Port Gellhorn motel. (Spoilers for Chapter 1.)

items.title: Inside GTA VI's fursuit ban and the Furverts rescue
items.summary: Kotaku explains Leonida's fursuit ban, the TV spots urging people to report furries and the hunters licensed to shoot them — and why the game itself is sympathetic rather than hostile: a roadside encounter lets you rescue a fox-suited character and drive members of the underground Furverts to safety, and Jason and Lucia can text that furries are misunderstood, though nothing stops a player choosing violence after collecting the reward.

items.title: Guide: flip your car back over by hand
items.summary: Polygon explains you cannot right a flipped vehicle from inside in GTA VI: get out, walk against its middle until the shove prompt appears, then hold Square on PS5 or X on Xbox until it is upright — it only works on fully upended cars, boats and larger vehicles, not planes, and not if an obstacle blocks the other side.

items.title: Guide: get your car out of the police impound
items.summary: Polygon outlines two ways to recover an impounded car: sneak into the lot and steal it back, then escape the police, or from Chapter 2 use the Scooter Bros app to pay a distance-based fee — an example $699 from Vice City to Port Gellhorn — or spend Premium daily credits.

items.title: Guide: reveal the whole Leonida map from the air
items.summary: Polygon recommends clearing Leonida's fog from the air in a plane or helicopter, ideally the fuel-efficient Mammoth Dodo seaplane found near coastal hangars, swapping aircraft when fuel runs low, checking fuel with down on the D-pad, and avoiding lingering over yellow-tinted restricted sites like Mile Zero Air Station and VCIA.

items.title: Only 40% of GTA VI players have cleared Chapter 2 so far
items.summary: Polygon reports trophy and achievement data showing most players are taking it slow: 66.22% on PS5 have finished Chapter 1 and only 40.55% have cleared Chapter 2, with 6.45% past Chapter 3 and 0.88% past the final mission, despite PS5 players averaging 17.4 hours by Nov. 23.

items.title: GTA VI now streams on PS5 and PlayStation Portal with PS Plus Premium
items.summary: Push Square reports GTA VI now supports PS Plus Premium cloud streaming directly to PS5 and PlayStation Portal, a feature that was not available at launch and which it tested working on a PS5 in the UK: Premium members who own a digital copy can stream it from Sony's servers instead of their own console, including on a Portal with no PS5 at home, though the game has not been added to the PS Plus catalogue itself.

items.title: Sony: GTA VI is the biggest launch in PlayStation history, with 39 million PS5 players
items.summary: Sony says GTA VI is the biggest game launch in PlayStation history across three decades and five console generations: more than 39 million unique players on PS5 between November 19 and 22, a new PlayStation record for concurrent players, 683 million hours played at 17.4 hours per player on average, and the most newly connected PS5 consoles in a single day since the system's 2020 launch outside the holidays, with GTA VI the first game played on 70% of those new consoles.

items.title: Guide: open the portal to the PS2-era Malibu Club and earn Tommy Vercetti's shirt
items.summary: Kotaku explains how to unlock the hidden trip back to 2002 that YouTuber Memeio first cracked: start at the tower in Key Lento, then work the switches at 12 LPL substations in the order of the old Vice City cheat 'Life Is Passing Me By' without fast travelling, follow the text message to Reactor 2 at the power plant between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m., and step through the portal into the PS2-era Malibu Club to find Kent Paul and return with Tommy Vercetti's blue Hawaiian shirt and a chopper motorcycle.

items.title: Rockstar releases GTA VI: The Album (Deluxe Edition) with 23 bonus tracks
items.summary: Rockstar announced the Deluxe Edition of the GTA VI album is out now on major streaming services, adding 23 bonus tracks with contributions from The Dare, Slayyyter, Denzel Curry, HEALTH, Power Trip, Real Dimez x Sexyy Red and more, on top of the original 34-track release.

items.title: Guide: find Port Gellhorn's missing tourists and its serial killer
items.summary: Polygon's guide starts the side mission from the missing-person posters in the Starlet Motel office after Chapter 2, sneaks into the warehouse across from Moses' garage for the photo clues, then tracks the three tourists — a pink car in the central Gelhorn junkyard, a car in the water at Wild Hog Point, and floorboards in a blue trailer at the north-end trailer park — before a return to the warehouse ends the hunt.

items.title: Guide: 'Dealer's Choice' pure vs. cut drugs outcomes explained
items.summary: Polygon explains the Chapter 3 choice for Dre'Quan and Tyrone: selling the pure drugs runs smoothly for $1,500 and a 'professional' profile bump, while the cut drugs anger the buyers — defusing at half price matches the clean outcome, but talking tough forces a shootout and police escape for the same $1,500 and a 'violent' profile bump.

items.title: Guide: find the Silent Hill hotel and open the Marbelle safe
items.summary: Polygon's guide sends you to the Marbelle Hotel in Crosstown, Vice City, beside Pizza Pete: enter by the east door and climb to the top floor to trigger the fog event, then open the desk safe with code 955214 — found on the staircase wall or in roof notes — for $234 and a Crowex Ambassador 'Breakfast' watch.
